full_judgment:
6. The petitioners have given a short background of the law relating to diluvion and alluvion of lands. By the East Bengal State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, 1950 (EB Act, No. XXVIII of 1951) the rent-receivers intervening between the Government and the actual occupants of the said land were abolished and such occupants became tenants directly under the Government subject to a ceiling as to the maximum area of land which a tenant could hold. Time to time the law relating to the tenant's right on his diluviated and alluviated land were passed. On 13-7-94 the State Acquisition and Tenancy (Amendment) Act, 1994 was promulgated substituting in place of the old section 86 with regard to abatement of rent on account of diluvion and determination of right in land re-appearing on account of alluvion. By the said Act, the right, title, interest of the original tenant or his successor-in-interest would subsist in the lands of a holding or portion thereof during the period of loss by diluvion if such lands re-appeared in situ within 30 years of their loss instead of 20 years. The respondent No. 1 by the impugned order issued to all the Deputy Commissioners of the Districts including Bhola directed them to take necessary steps for processing the diluvion and alluvion land and that all land already diluviated and alluviated shall vest in the Government and, as such, be recorded in the Khas-khatian of the government. The petitioners are aggrieved by the impugned circular/order because it is not in accordance with the State Acquisition and Tenancy (Amendment) Act, 1994 and the Revenue authorities in pursuance of the said memo refused to accept rents for the alluviated lands belonging to the petitioners in spite of repeated requests approaches. Hence, the petitioners are constrained to file this writ petition challenging the validity of the impugned order (Annexure-E) and obtained the present Rule. 

 9. Mr Mahmudul Islam, learned Senior Advocate with Mr AQM Safiullah, Advocate appearing for the writ petitioners, submits that before amendment as per section 86(4) of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, 1950 (EB Act, XXVIII of 1951) the petitioners' ownership subsisted, inasmuch as the lands of the above mouzas reappeared in 1993-94. While the ownership of the petitioners was continuing without any break and they were in exclusive possession,' there came the amendment of section 86 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, 1950 on 13-7-94 by the State Acquisition and Tenancy (Amendment) Act, 1994 (Act XV of 1994). He further submits that the impugned memo dated 29-11-1994 (Annexure-E) issued by the respondent No.1 giving illegal interpretation of the State Acquisition and Tenancy (Amendment) Act, 1994 (Act XV of 1994) directing the respondent No. 2, the Deputy Commissioner, Bhola not to give effect to the above Act of 1994 in respect of the lands which have been diluviated and alluviated before 13-7-1994 is wholly illegal, malafide, without jurisdiction, without lawful authority and is of no legal effect. It is further argued by him that section 86(2) of the State Acquisition and Tenancy (Amendment) Act, 1994 clearly envisages that the right, title, interest of the original tenant or his successors-in-interest shall subsist in the lands of a holding or portion thereof during the period of loss by diluvion if such lands re-appear in situ within 30 years of their loss and that the impugned memo dated 29-11-94 is contrary to the decision of the Appellate Division of the Supreme Court of Bangladesh reported in 31 DLR (AD) 195 wherein it was held that the proprietary right of the person to whom the land belonged and during the period of submergence of the land the ownership is not lost but merely suspended and on its re- appearance in its old site the owner gets it back. 

 12. The petitioner's case is that by the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, 1994 (Act XV of 1994) the right, title, interest in their lands lost by diluvion has been restored and on its re-appearance they are entitled to get its allotment subject to ceiling imposed by the Act as tenant of the land. If the impugned order is not interfered with their right of ownership which has been restored by the Act, 1994 would be taken away. It is also submitted that the respondents have misconstrued both the provisions of President's Order No. 135 of 1972 and the Act of 1994 which amended section 86 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act of 1950.
